findings.summary: Frozen rows label menu-derived arrays as official ingredients or official product-allergen evidence, but the independently reopened sources provide menu names/descriptions only. Toast remains restaurant-linked vendor evidence; the official PDFs are menus, not allergen matrices or complete ingredient documents. Complete arrays, negative semantics, and may-contain assertions cannot be verified.

The accessible current menu boundary is incomplete: official Linner and Ready To-Go image surfaces cannot be enumerated, and Toast, weekday PDF, and brunch PDF scopes differ. Therefore the sources cannot establish product removals, complete menu negatives, or restaurant-wide cross-contact semantics.

The frozen catalog contains duplicate, stale, generic, and service-period-dependent presentations. Examples include All Beef Dog versus All Beef Hot Dog, J. Baker/J. Baker's Pimiento Cheese variants, Blackened Turkey Meatballs variants, old variant labels, and products absent from current accessible surfaces. Parser or source reconciliation requires adjudication before any repair.

The only narrow process statement found is that beignets are fried in 100% refined peanut oil. It is not a complete ingredient list, a restaurant-wide allergen statement, or a cross-contact disclosure; no may-contain conclusion is supported.

summary: Low-confidence discrepancy result. All three scout menu surfaces were verified exactly once. The scout supplied zero currentProductKeys, so currentProductCheckGroups is intentionally empty; the accessible Toast food/nonalcoholic catalog is reported only once as an additional discovery and is not misrepresented as a scout product. All 83 frozen auditItemKeys are reconciled exactly once. Multiple current menu surfaces, incomplete scope, source-authority gaps, stale/variant catalog drift, and unresolved cross-contact semantics require Sol adjudication.
